"import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Font

# Create a new workbook (Sheet1)
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Sheet1"

# Title above the answer region
ws['A13'] = "VBA Macro for Excel 2016 - Remove Alphabetic Characters from Column B"
ws['A13'].font = Font(bold=True, size=12)

# VBA Macro Code - the answer to be placed in A14:I137
macro_code = """Sub RemoveAlphaCharacters()
' Purpose: Removes alphabetic characters from cell values in column B,
'          keeping only numeric digits. Preserves date values.
'
' Handles patterns like:
'   "PID1"   -> "1"
'   "PID2"   -> "2"
'   "GG 1"   -> "1"
'   "AB12"   -> "12"
'   "XYZ 5"  -> "5"
'
' Date values in the column are left unchanged.

    Dim ws As Worksheet
    Dim cell As Range
    Dim lastRow As Long
    Dim cellValue As Variant
    Dim numericPart As String
    
    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    lastRow = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, "B").End(xlUp).Row
    
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    
    For Each cell In ws.Range("B1:B" & lastRow)
        cellValue = cell.Value
        
        ' Skip empty cells
        If IsEmpty(cell) Or Len(Trim(CStr(cellValue))) = 0 Then
            GoTo NextCell
        End If
        
        ' Skip date values - preserve them as-is
        If IsDate(cellValue) Then
            GoTo NextCell
        End If
        
        ' Only process text strings (alphanumeric codes)
        If VarType(cellValue) = vbString Then
            numericPart = ExtractDigits(cellValue)
            If numericPart <> "" Then
                cell.Value = numericPart
            End If
        End If
        
NextCell:
    Next cell
    
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    
    MsgBox "Macro complete. Processed " & lastRow & " rows in column B.", vbInformation
End Sub

Function ExtractDigits(inputStr As String) As String
' Helper function: removes all alphabetic characters and whitespace
' from inputStr, returning only the numeric digits.
'
    Dim regex As Object
    Set regex = CreateObject("VBScript.RegExp")
    
    regex.Pattern = "[A-Za-z\s]+"
    regex.Global = True
    
    ExtractDigits = regex.Replace(inputStr, "")
End Function

' HOW TO USE:
' 1. Open your workbook in Excel 2016.
' 2. Press ALT+F11 to open the Visual Basic Editor (VBE).
' 3. Insert > Module, then paste the code above into the module.
' 4. Close the VBE (ALT+Q).
' 5. On the worksheet, press ALT+F8, select "RemoveAlphaCharacters",
'    and click "Run".
'
' Notes:
' - The macro only modifies cells in column B that contain text strings.
' - Empty cells are ignored.
' - Any cell whose value is recognised by IsDate() (true date or a
'   date-like string) is left untouched.
' - For alphanumeric strings such as "PID1", "GG 1", "AB12" the macro
'   replaces the cell content with just the digits ("1", "1", "12").
' - A reference to "Microsoft VBScript Regular Expressions 5.5" is
'   required; it is included with Excel 2016 by default, so no extra
'   setup is needed.
"""

# Write each line of the macro into column A starting at row 14
for i, line in enumerate(macro_code.split('\n')):
    row = 14 + i
    if row > 137:
        break
    ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=line)

# Save the workbook as output.xlsx
wb.save('output.xlsx')
print("output.xlsx created successfully with the VBA macro in A14:I137")"
